title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 89 (Declaration of beneficial interest)

content.overview: Section 89 requires (i) a registered holder who is not the beneficial owner and (ii) the beneficial owner whose name is not entered in the register to make prescribed declarations, generally within thirty days of the relevant entry/acquisition; changes must also be declared within thirty days. The company must note the declaration in its register and file the prescribed return with the Registrar within thirty days of receipt. Rights in shares may be unenforceable by the beneficial owner if the required declaration is not made, but the company's dividend obligation is preserved.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 89 (Declaration in respect of beneficial interest in any share). A person whose name is entered in the register of members but who does not hold the beneficial interest must declare that fact and the prescribed particulars to the company within thirty days of the relevant entry. A person who holds or acquires a beneficial interest in shares but whose name is not entered in the register must declare the nature of the interest and particulars to the company within thirty days of acquiring it. Where the beneficial interest changes, the registered holder and beneficial owner must make the prescribed declarations within thirty days of the change. The company must note the declaration in the relevant register and file the prescribed return with the Registrar within thirty days of receipt. If the beneficial owner fails to make a required declaration, rights in the shares may not be enforceable by that person or anyone claiming through them. The section does not prejudice the company's obligation to pay dividends to its members; payment discharges that obligation. The official consolidated text also states a separate penalty for company failure to file the return, but its application should be checked against current amendments and section 403. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Registered holder without beneficial interest
sections.body: A person whose name is entered in the register of members but who does not hold the beneficial interest must make the prescribed declaration to the company, stating the fact and particulars of the beneficial owner, within thirty days of the relevant entry.

sections.heading: Beneficial owner not registered
sections.body: A person who holds or acquires a beneficial interest in shares but whose name is not entered in the register of members must declare the nature of the interest and prescribed particulars to the company within thirty days of acquiring the beneficial interest.

sections.heading: Change in beneficial interest
sections.body: Where the beneficial interest in shares changes, the registered holder and beneficial owner must make the prescribed declarations within thirty days of the change.

sections.heading: Company register and Registrar filing
sections.body: The company must note the declaration in the relevant register and file the prescribed return with the Registrar within thirty days of receiving the declaration, in the prescribed form and with the prescribed fees/additional fees.

sections.heading: Effect of non-declaration and dividends
sections.body: Rights in a share for which a required declaration has not been made by the beneficial owner are not enforceable by that person or anyone claiming through them. This does not prejudice the company's obligation to pay dividends to its members; on payment, that obligation is discharged.

sections.heading: Penalty for company filing default
sections.body: The official consolidated text states a separate penalty for a company required to file the subsection (6) return that fails to do so, including a fine and continuing-default fine. Because this provision references section 403 and penalty amendments must be reconciled, confirm the current consolidated wording before applying an amount to a real matter.

examples.body: A person whose name is entered as a holder, but who does not hold the beneficial interest, and the person who holds that interest, must declare it.

hypotheticals.question: A person's name is entered in the register of members, but another person holds the beneficial interest. What does section 89 require?
hypotheticals.analysis: The registered holder must make the prescribed declaration to the company, identifying the fact that the holder is not the beneficial owner and providing the required particulars. The declaration is generally due within thirty days of the relevant entry.

hypotheticals.question: A beneficial owner does not make the required declaration. What consequence does section 89 state for rights in the shares?
hypotheticals.analysis: Rights in the shares may not be enforceable by the beneficial owner or anyone claiming through that person. The section separately preserves the company's obligation to pay dividends to its members.

distinctions.title: Section 89 beneficial interest and section 90 significant beneficial ownership
distinctions.left: Section 89 requires declarations by a registered holder who is not the beneficial owner and by the beneficial owner not entered in the register.
distinctions.right: Section 90 addresses significant beneficial owners, including indirect holdings/control, and imposes additional company identification/register/return duties.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming section 89 imposes no time limit.
misconceptions.correction: The relevant declarations and changes are generally due within thirty days under the respective subsections.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the registered holder and beneficial owner as the same person in every case.
misconceptions.correction: Section 89 expressly addresses cases where the registered holder does not hold the beneficial interest and where the beneficial owner is not registered.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming non-declaration automatically extinguishes the company's dividend obligation.
misconceptions.correction: The section expressly preserves the company's obligation to pay dividends to its members.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 89 require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A person whose name is entered as a holder, but who does not hold the beneficial interest, and the person who holds that interest, must declare it.
